method: Static byte inspection, PE resource extraction, Rizin and Capstone control-flow tracing; no sample execution.

samples.identification: StormAttack installer/injector with Storm Ser DLL; collector Elex/Remcos/WannaCry labels are not the identification evidence.
evidence: Outer 0x401150 launches a process, writes a DLL path into remote memory and passes resolved LoadLibraryA to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
Outer 0x401260 writes the LanmanServer ServiceDll replacement; 0x401900 constructs an Active Setup component and writes StubPath at 0x401a4b.
Outer contains shell cleanup/self-delete; embedded DLL starts at file offset 0x5060 and carries Storm DDOS Server / Storm Ser DLL identity resources.
DLL 0x10006ac9 selects/receives up to 0x528 bytes, copies a 0x14a-dword record and dispatches its first dword at 0x10006b71.
DLL 0x1000228e creates AF_INET/SOCK_RAW/IPPROTO_UDP, then 0x10002353 sends twelve datagrams per burst and repeats until the stop flag changes.
Packet opcode 5 invokes 0x100067c2; the task string is tokenized into download arguments, an API is resolved and called, and the staged path reaches CreateProcessA at 0x10006917.
Packet opcodes 7, 8 and 18 reach handlers 0x100065a4, 0x10006549 and 0x100065ff. These enable SeShutdownPrivilege and call ExitWindowsEx with flags 9, 2 and 4, respectively.
samples.obfuscation: Embedded DLL places code and imports in a writable .data section without execute permission; manual injection explains the nonstandard layout. Code is directly recoverable; no encrypted command layer was established.
samples.coverage: All eight existing hostile observations across outer and embedded PE retained; added packet-controlled privileged shutdown API objective.
samples.context_missing: No operator identity, deployment authorization or runtime success was observed. Implant tasking, traffic attacks, service replacement and injection outweigh a hypothetical authorized test.
samples.marker_line: StormAttack: DDoS, injection and persistence; add shutdown coverage

samples.identification: zzhelloworld_socktest RubyGem 0.2.0, author claim derekiops, summary test gem do not use.
evidence: Loading lib/zzhelloworld_socktest.rb evaluates the module body directly, opens TCPSocket.new to 66.78.40.218:32768, reopens STDIN, STDOUT and STDERR on that socket, then execs /bin/sh -i.
No opt-in entry point, authentication, caller-selected endpoint or normal library function surrounds the shell. This is require-time execution, not a gem-install hook.
README is a mostly inert HTML parser test corpus and generated gem boilerplate; xss.svg only calls alert(0x539). Neither explains away the Ruby execution path.
Version file says 0.2.0; Rakefile contains ordinary Bundler/RSpec/RuboCop tasks. No fetched dependency supplies the hostile code.
samples.obfuscation: Plain Ruby, no concealment needed to establish the shell.
samples.coverage: One hostile reverse-shell trait and one suspicious socket/shell trait retained on the gem, data.tar.gz and Ruby member. Output reopening now includes stderr; parsed call shape excludes quoted/commented examples.
samples.minimum_coverage_gap: Only one distinct hostile behavior is supported: a reverse shell. A second hostile rule would duplicate that behavior; the accompanying suspicious rule is preserved without inventing another objective.
samples.context_missing: Research-test branding is plausible but no bounded local test or user authorization is supplied. The executable hard-coded public reverse shell controls the judgement.

classifier.disagreement: ML misses the malicious Ruby member despite the hostile behavioral trait; the outer gem is correctly alerted.

samples.marker_line: Socktest 0.2.0: require-time reverse shell; cover stderr redirection

samples.identification: Yandex lite_installer 24.4.3.1012, x86 Windows browser installer.
evidence: Version fields, CI PDB path and YANDEX LLC signer agree. Current Authenticode content hash equals signed SHA256 608647e7ebb96ec9bd3c2aa48ae171894fa1989753565d81b5feba25aefa6b8b.

osslsigncode independently reproduces that content-hash equality and the timestamp verification. Its final chain verification fails on the extra Dummy certificate / local trust chain, so this review does not claim an independently trusted full certificate chain.

Large resources were extracted. BIN/320 is an MSZip CAB containing partner_config, resources/tablo and resources/configs/all_zip; ABT_CONFIG is JSON. Other dominant resources are actual JPEG/PNG images and TrueType fonts, rather than encrypted executable payloads.
0x435e90 reads resources and copies them into a GlobalAlloc-backed stream; 0x438230 returns a resource pointer and size; 0x4a4bf0 copies resource data into a vector.

0x4e0764 walks this image’s section headers to locate the delay-import area. 0x4e08bc requests PAGE_READWRITE (4), and 0x4e08ef restores the old protection through 0x4e084e. This is delay-import support, without resource-to-code execution.
IsDebuggerPresent at 0x4e00e0 gates an ATL critical-section initialization error diagnostic; other references belong to exception/CRT handling, not a demonstrated anti-analysis gate.

ShellExecuteExW at 0x4291a1 and 0x47cd1e uses runas for installer elevation. CreateProcessW at 0x4211dd is RunModuleAndWait; the code logs setup process exit status. No cmd.exe/shell stage is established by ShellExecuteEx.

The unsigned trailing 2048-byte tag begins Yact and contains installation attribution/configuration query fields and zero padding. A PE checksum mismatch is present, while the signed content digest still matches.
No traced path supports Expiro-style grafting, file infection, backdoor dispatch, stealing or surveillance. API/entropy co-occurrence alone cannot supply those effects.
samples.coverage: Four hostile composites relocated with identical predicates, size gates and exclusions into notable capability profiles. Both resource-label atoms relocated out of masquerade and their exact consumers updated. Every other finding retained.
samples.context_missing: Original download route, user consent and eventual remote installer response were not supplied. The signed code and traced installation paths support likely benign software; browser promotion/attribution alone is not malware.

classifier.remaining_disagreement: No alert at the default calibrated level after correction; individual native model probability remains 0.7096892 and is not the final aggregate decision.

samples.marker_line: Yandex installer: signed normal setup; fix four hostile inferences

unsupported_claims: Resource entropy plus WinHTTP and VirtualProtect proves neither encrypted resources nor execution of downloaded bytes.
Resource API lookup, protection, process enumeration and process creation establish no linked resource-to-process payload or injection.
Resource APIs plus ShellExecuteEx and IsDebuggerPresent establish neither a misleading identity nor encryption, shell execution, backdoor or evasive gating.
MZ/PE constants, checksum mismatch, high-entropy resources and VirtualProtect are normal parser/runtime operations and do not identify Expiro or prove infection.
rule_review.preservation: All four predicates/exclusions are retained as notable neutral composites. No product, signer, filename or dependency exception was introduced. Genuine Expiro delta-stub and infection rules remain unchanged.
rule_review.placement: WinHTTP profile -> communications/http/client/winhttp; memory protection with resource/process API context -> mem/protect/modify; resource/ShellExecute profile -> process/create/shellexec; PE validation profile -> data/format/pe-parser; Yandex resource labels -> metadata/binary/resource/identity.
rule_review.consumers: Exact and ancestor references audited. Four former hostile IDs had no consumers. The two resource-label exact consumers in installer masquerade and Cobalt Strike were updated. Destination ancestor effects were compared through whole-report regression; no unrelated findings changed.
rule_review.ruby_matcher: The call facts expose only the basename reopen and no receiver, so receiver-sensitive tree-sitter queries are used. They retain actual stdin/stdout variable-stream calls, add stderr and reject strings/comments. The reverse-shell consumer accepts stdin plus either output channel.

regression.controls: Six parsed Ruby controls plus an ExitWindowsEx-import mutation of the real StormAttack sample; original samples and all archive members compared before/after.

external_positive_controls.evidence: Fetched with forager by digest. Embedded image at 0x4064 has RWX .rsrc entropy 7.9923. At embedded offset 4300800 / VA 0xaf8000, register saves and call/pop/sub delta setup lead into XOR/sub/add/not transformations of the body. Expiro resource-delta infection and WannaCry detections retained on all three analyzed units.
Fetched with forager by digest; large RWX .reloc entropy 7.9402. All existing relocation/carrier findings unchanged. Feed identity is a lead, not proof of a particular payload.
Fetched with forager by digest; UPX0/UPX1 image. All observations on outer and embedded units unchanged; no family inference from the feed alone.

regression.external_artifacts: Original bytes and .forage.json provenance are retained under scratch/review/expiro-control, not checked in.
regression.material_detection_losses: None after accounting for the documented ID relocations and correction of four unsupported hostile severities. All original true-positive hostile/suspicious findings on StormAttack, the gem and external controls remain.
regression.limitations: Static behavior and capability are established, not runtime success. The Triage links were unavailable through the web tool.
regression.matcher_preservation: Four composite predicate/exclusion equivalence checks passed against git HEAD baseline; effective PE/DLL and Windows scopes preserved.
